text: Metadata Management & Business Glossary gave you the vocabulary and the inventory. This course goes deep on the next layer: lineage — the recorded path data takes from where it starts to everywhere it ends up.

A plain definition — 'tracking where data comes from' — misses the part that matters most: every transformation in between. The sharper version: lineage lets you retrace, step by step, exactly how a number got to be the number you're looking at, and exactly what else would be affected if any step in that chain changed.

A shipped package gets scanned at every stage — pickup, sorting facility, truck, delivery. The tracking page isn't the package, it's the recorded path it took. Data lineage does the same job: a source system, an extraction job, a transformation step, a warehouse load, a semantic model, a dashboard. Each arrow is a hop.

You already use lineage thinking. A bank wire's trail — sent from one account, cleared through an intermediary, deposited to another. A document's version history — who changed what, and when. A food label's sourcing trail — grown here, processed there, packaged somewhere else. All three let you retrace an origin.

Twenty-four more lessons ahead: why lineage matters, business versus technical lineage, column versus table granularity, and the standards that keep it consistent — then four more chapters tracing real systems, dependencies, documentation, and applied practice. Next lesson: why lineage matters, and what actually breaks without it.
